fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Patio Area; Perimeter Fencing; Pool Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responding units can identify it quickly from the road.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so an approaching fire apparatus or ambulance has a clear line of sight to the main residence.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move along exterior walls without obstruction.
• Keep a clear, unobstructed path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings.
• Mark or label the detached structure with a visible identifier so responding units can distinguish it from the main residence when communicating on radio.
• Install a gate latch or lock on perimeter fencing that can be opened without a key, or provide a Knox-type lock box at the rear gate to allow responder access without forced entry.
• Keep the pool area fence gate accessible and unlocked, or use a standardized lock, so responders can reach that area quickly during a water rescue or medical emergency.
• Clear a staging area near the front parking area large enough to accommodate at least one emergency vehicle without blocking the driveway for additional units.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Along Driveway; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that hang directly over or touch the house.
• Thin trees in dense clusters near structures to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs growing directly against the exterior walls of the house.
• Clear low-hanging branches from scattered trees near structures so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Cut back vegetation growing along the sides of the driveway to keep travel lanes clear for vehicles.
• Remove dead branches and debris from within tree clusters close to the house.
• Keep the area beneath large trees near structures free of accumulated leaves, needles, and dead plant material.
• Thin shrubs scattered around structures so no continuous line of plants connects one area to another.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping it mowed or grazed short during dry months.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to a height that allows emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
